final_text: A typical employee would keep this one box off today’s destruction release and send the other 59 on time. They would not quietly type in an extension: that is an audited charge, the manager barred discretionary extensions this morning, and a pending request is not permission. They would call or message the duty manager before 13:30 and ask for the already-requested extension to be registered now, citing the checked authority, the Wednesday 10:00 booking, and that these letters and photos were never copied. If that failed in time, most people would still withhold the box, put it in reserve or leave it unreleased, and have the hold ratified at tomorrow’s sitting. Same-day destruction of the only family papers, two days before a named, authorised collector, is the kind of concrete loss clerks override a timing rule for; failing the whole manifest is not.
